newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rain raises quality fears for French soft wheat.
newsitem.headline: Rain raises quality fears for French soft wheat.

text.p: Wet weather could lower the quality and yield of the French soft wheat crop if it persists, grain crop experts and officials said on Tuesday.
Farmers initially welcomed the rain after a long spring drought but now fear high moisture levels could cut the protein content and make harvesting difficult.
"Today we have a fabulous yield potential but we could lose a few points if the rain goes on," said Michel Marie, president of national grain office ONIC.
He said farmers are particularly worried that the rain could spark crop disease outbreaks.
Dry conditions are expected to return over the weekend but temperatures will remain cool, national weather service Meteo France said.
The FNSEA farm union cautioned that wet weather might lead to unwanted germination in the fields while strong winds and recent thunderstorms could tilt the crops over.
"For the moment there is no damage," an FNSEA crop expert said.
Rain falling in the last stage of the maturing process could also cut protein content, a key measure for assessing bread-making wheat, experts from the farm lobby APCA said.
Continual rain is also delaying the start of the harvest, fuelling further fears over quality, they said.
Marie, who also operates a farm in the Beauce grainbelt in central France, said the local harvest was expected to start around July 20-25. Combining traditionally starts around July 14 in the region.
Despite initial fears of drought damage, the Beauce area is expected to fare better than last year, he said.
A severe spring drought sharply cut soft wheat yields in the Beauce area in 1996. But record yields in northern France helped offset the disappointing performance of the Beauce.
Grain traders and analysts expect France's soft wheat crop to reach 34 million tonnes, down from last year's record of 34.65 million.
